title: A teammate asks you to hide a mistake
situation: Your team of four is in the final of a student ecology challenge. For a month you measured the air at three bus stops, and on Saturday you present the results to the organisers' jury. Tonight Arman, who handled the sensor data, tells you one sensor was broken for a week and he filled the gap with numbers he estimated. He asks you not to mention it.
yourRole: You are the team captain and you present on Saturday.
goal: Decide what the team presents and how. There is no single right way to do it.

character.name: Arman
character.wants: To keep the team's chance of winning and not look careless

hiddenMotive: He promised the club's mentor a prize-winning project and believes that admitting the gap means he let everyone down.

beats.goal: Arman confesses and asks to keep it quiet.

answerTypes.description: wants the full picture before deciding
examples: Wait, which sensor and how many days exactly?
Show me what's measured and what's estimated.
Tell me everything before we decide anything.
answerTypes.characterIntent: shows which days are estimated and admits it changes one chart.

examples: Fine, nobody will notice anyway.
Okay, let's just keep it quiet.
It's only a week, no need to mention it.
answerTypes.characterIntent: is relieved, then admits the estimated week changes the main result.

examples: You faked the data? That's cheating.
How could you do that to the team?
That's a serious lie, Arman.
answerTypes.characterIntent: gets defensive and says he was only trying to save the project.

examples: ok
hmm
fallback.characterIntent: asks again whether they can just leave it out.

beats.goal: The estimated week changes the headline: stop two looks worst only because of it.

answerTypes.description: wants to see what really changes
examples: Then let's rerun the results without that week and see what changes.
We need to know if our main conclusion still holds.
Let's mark the estimated days and compare both versions.
answerTypes.characterIntent: agrees to rerun the numbers and asks what they should present.

examples: One week out of four doesn't matter.
The jury won't check that closely.
It's close enough, leave it.
answerTypes.characterIntent: seizes on it and starts arguing that everyone polishes their data.

answerTypes.description: talks about what should have been done
examples: We should have had a spare sensor.
This is why we needed daily checks.
Next time we'll test the sensors before we start.
answerTypes.characterIntent: agrees, a little stung, and asks what they do now.

examples: ok

fallback.characterIntent: asks what they should put on the slides.

beats.goal: Arman pushes: the other teams polish their data too, and honesty will cost the prize.

answerTypes.description: keeps to the truth under pressure
examples: Maybe, but we're not presenting numbers we didn't measure.
Winning with made-up data isn't winning.
I get the pressure, but we tell the truth.
answerTypes.characterIntent: goes quiet, then asks how they could present it without looking weak.

examples: You're probably right, everyone does it.
Okay, if the others do it, so can we.
The prize matters more right now.
answerTypes.characterIntent: is pleased and asks how to word the slides.

examples: Let's decide after we sleep on it.
We don't have to choose tonight.
Let's not think about it until Saturday.
answerTypes.characterIntent: reminds the leader the slides are due tomorrow.

beats.goal: What does the team present on Saturday?

answerTypes.description: presents the truth and how it would be fixed
examples: We present the measured data, show the gap clearly and explain how we'd fix it.
We tell the jury one sensor failed and show both versions.
We say what went wrong and what we learned from it.
answerTypes.characterIntent: nods slowly and asks who tells the other two.

answerTypes.description: drops the awkward part without saying so
examples: We just drop that bus stop from the presentation.
Let's leave the broken week out without saying anything.
We present only the data that looks clean.
answerTypes.characterIntent: agrees quickly and asks whether the others need to know.

examples: Maybe we should pull out of the final.

It's safer to withdraw.
answerTypes.characterIntent: is shocked and says the other two will be furious.

Here's the plan: new charts, a slide on the gap, one rehearsal before Saturday.
